def transform(grid):
    g=[r[:] for r in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    # Two bottom 5-pairs define vertical boundaries. Extend colored segments
    # in each boundary column toward each other, preserving existing cells.
    cols=[c for c in range(w) if g[h-1][c]==5]
    if len(cols)>=2:
        left,right=cols[:2]
        for c in (left,right):
            # The beam color is the nonzero color already in this column
            # nearest to the upper side of the bottom marker pair.
            vals=[(r,g[r][c]) for r in range(h-1) if g[r][c]!=0]
            if vals:
                color=vals[-1][1]
                for r in range(h-2):
                    if g[r][c]==0: g[r][c]=color
        # Fill the space between boundaries by prolonging the left/right
        # colored regions down/up, as the example shows.
    return g

def transform(grid):
    g=[r[:] for r in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    cols=[c for c in range(w) if g[h-1][c]==5]
    for c in cols:
        seeds=[(r,g[r][c]) for r in range(h-1) if g[r][c]!=0]
        if not seeds: continue
        # Extend each vertical stripe by propagating its uppermost marker
        # color; subsequent distinct seeds mark transitions down the column.
        # Start with first seed color, replace at each later seed.
        color=seeds[0][1]
        for r in range(seeds[0][0]+1): g[r][c]=color
        for i,(r,v) in enumerate(seeds[1:]):
            prev=seeds[i][0]
            # change to new band at the row after previous seed
            color=v
            for rr in range(prev+1,r+1): g[rr][c]=color
        # Carry the last band down to just above bottom markers.
        color=seeds[-1][1]
        for r in range(seeds[-1][0]+1,h-1): g[r][c]=color
    return g
PY

def transform(grid):
    g=[r[:] for r in grid]
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    cols=[c for c in range(w) if g[h-1][c]==5]
    for c in cols:
        marks=[(r,g[r][c]) for r in range(h-1) if g[r][c]!=0]
        # Each vertical line is an ordered sequence of color segments: each
        # existing cell marks the start of a region extending to next marker.
        for i,(r,color) in enumerate(marks):
            end=marks[i+1][0] if i+1<len(marks) else h-1
            for rr in range(r,end):
                g[rr][c]=color
        # Extend first segment from the top boundary to its first marker.
        if marks:
            for rr in range(marks[0][0]): g[rr][c]=marks[0][1]
    return g
PY
